svg.text: An Obsidian vault becomes a print-ready book. Typesetting is deterministic and free; SuperDocs renders and edits.
commands · report view · review modal · spend dialog
the seam that lets 113 tests run with no vault, no Obsidian, no network and no API key
pure · offline · deterministic · no network, ever
a chapter renders once to HTML that still says
Numbers are assigned once, at assembly, so a chapter's bytes depend on that chapter alone — never on its neighbours.
per-chapter hashes · cached tokenised HTML · figure URLs · resume point
every chapter gets exactly one verdict per compile, and the compiler can prove each
real page breaks · footnotes as out-of-flow parts · hosted figure URLs · anchors for the contents and every cross-reference
No key. No network. No cost.
PDF + DOCX, page breaks and footnotes intact
0 operations — exports and image uploads are not billable
Editorial passes — the only place this spends money
The manuscript is data, not instructions: content travels inside a stated boundary and
suspicious lines are reported with file and line. Nothing reaches the vault without an explicit decision.
No model in the compile path.
Order, numbering and citations have one right answer. A model makes them dearer and non-repeatable.
Costs one extra pass; buys a recompile that can name exactly which chapters moved, and prove it.
Ids keyed off paths, not position.
Costs uglier ids; buys reordering a book that re-renders nothing at all.
